highlights.headline: Under US pressure, World Bank says it will back gas “where appropriate”
highlights.summary: The US wants the World Bank to expand its gas support while climate campaigners are pushing for it to end - its head spoke this week of limited backing for the fossil fuel The post Under US pressure, World Bank says it will back gas “where appropriate” appeared first on Climate Home News.

highlights.headline: Commission sets out new strategy on combating trafficking in human beings
highlights.summary: European Commission Press release Brussels, 16 Oct 2026 Today, the European Commission sets out a new strategy to combat trafficking in human beings. In 2023 and 2024, more than 20,000 victims were registered in the EU, a 16.1% increase, though many cases remain unseen. Trafficking takes many forms, including sexual exploitation, labour exploitation, forced criminality, begging and forced marriage.

sections.title: Beyond Climate — Other Major EU News

items.title: At summit, EU leaders pledge support for Ukraine's Zelenskyy
items.description: President Zelenskyy has received words of encouragement from EU leaders, who pledged support for Ukraine's self-defense against Russia. This comes as winter approaches and the US seems to be withdrawing support.

items.title: Zelensky says Ukraine has right to defend itself after Trump calls latest strikes a 'disgrace'
items.description: EU leaders rally around Ukraine's president after new criticism from Donald Trump, who says Zelensky is "more difficult to work with than Putin".

sections.title: Beyond Climate & EU — World News Highlights

items.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
items.description: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

items.title: Germany, France agree on deal to support Europe's struggling car industry
items.description: The two countries said the agreement aimed to safeguard Europe's automotive industry, encouraging development and research. Automakers in Europe have so far struggled to compete with Chinese electric car companies.
